help: sqlite uses a private database file in this node's storage. postgresql connects to the server configured below.
query reads rows in a read-only transaction. execute, insert_rows and upsert write data and need allow_writes.
One statement. Bind message values with :name or %(name)s placeholders; values are never inserted into the SQL text.
Target table, optionally schema.table. Names are quoted exactly as written.
JSON array of column names. Every params object must provide each of them (null allowed); other keys are ignored.
Columns of the unique key used by ON CONFLICT, e.g. ["sku"].
Columns updated on conflict. Empty updates every non-conflict column; all columns as conflict columns means DO NOTHING.
Writes stay disabled until this is checked. Each message is applied in one transaction: all of it or nothing.
File name inside this node's storage, ending in .sqlite3, .sqlite or .db. No folders, links or ATTACH.
Server host name, IP address or absolute Unix-socket directory. Nothing is contacted until a message arrives.
Server port, usually 5432.
Database name.
Database role. Use a role with only the privileges this node needs.
Wallet reference such as secret://workspace/pg_app, never the password itself. Empty sends no password.
TLS mode. verify-full checks the certificate and host name. disable is accepted only for local connections.
Optional named statements, e.g. {"init":{"operation":"execute","sql":"CREATE TABLE ..."}}. Select one with {"$statement":"init","$params":{...}}.
Deadline for connecting, locks and every statement of one message. Stop interrupts the running statement.
Maximum rows published on the rows output.
Maximum size of the published rows, in bytes.
When a limit is exceeded, publish the first rows with truncated true instead of failing.
Maximum parameter objects in one array message.
Maximum size of one params message, in bytes.
The SQLite file cannot grow beyond this size; a write that would exceed it fails and is rolled back.
Optional CA certificate: an absolute PEM file path, or system for the system store (libpq 16+). Empty uses the libpq default.
